sources: FAO-56 section on rice (land prep ~200 mm, ponding 50-100 mm)
FAO Irrigation Paper 33/IRRI: percolation 1-5 mm/d on heavy clay
Mekong alluvial paddy studies (Can Tho Univ.)
limitations: Percolation 2 mm/day is a mid value for heavy clay; varies 1-5 mm/day by soil and water table.
Land prep 200 mm is the FAO-56 standard, not locally measured.
Ponding depths are agronomic guidance, not field-specific.

soil_prior.notes_vi: Đất phù sa sét điển hình ĐBSCL; vùng phèn pH thấp hơn. Đây là giá trị vùng (prior), không phải đo tại ruộng.
sources: Vietnamese Mekong soil surveys (SIWRP / Can Tho Univ.)
limitations: Regional prior only; replace with field soil data when available.
TAW 150 mm/m is a mid value; acid sulfate soils have pH down to ~3.5-4.5.

salinity_season.affected_zone_note_vi: Ven biển: Bến Tre, Sóc Trăng, Trà Vinh, Cà Mau, Bạc Liêu, Tiền Giang, Kiên Giang; mặn xâm nhập đỉnh cuối mùa khô (tháng 3-5).
limitations: Dates are multi-year typical; actual onset and peak shift with El Nino years and upstream discharge.
Applies to coastal zones only; inland sites have negligible risk.

sources: MARD/Cuc Trong trot cropping calendars for Mekong Delta (Đông Xuân Nov-Dec, Hè Thu Mar-May, Thu Đông Jul-Aug)
limitations: Windows are widened to guarantee a 3-crop rice sequence: latest sowing + 110 d + 10 d turnaround fits the next window's end; actual local calendars vary by province and flood/salinity status.
Upland crops in Hè Thu face rain onset in May; their duration must be checked per sowing date.
